rationales: G1 is primarily for cell growth and preparation for DNA replication.
G2 is for growth and preparation for mitosis after DNA has replicated.
G0 is a resting state in which cells are not actively preparing to divide.
Chromosomes are duplicated during the S phase of interphase.
Palaeontology is the study of fossils.
Taxonomy is the science of naming and classifying organisms.
Parasitology is the study of parasites.
Immunology is the study of the immune system.
Orders are groups of related families, not families themselves.
Species are grouped into genera, not directly into families.
A family is a group of related genera.
Classes are groups of related orders.
Centrioles are membrane-free but are not the intended structures found in prokaryotes.
Vacuoles are membrane-bound structures and are generally absent from prokaryotes.
Mitochondria are membrane-bound organelles absent from prokaryotes.
Ribosomes are not membrane-bound and are found in prokaryotes.
Mitosis was not discovered in the 1890s.
The discovery is generally dated to the 1870s, not the 1880s.
Mitosis was first observed by Walther Flemming in the 1870s.
Mitosis was not discovered in the 1860s.
Animals undergo meiosis to produce haploid sex cells.
Plants undergo meiosis as part of their life cycle.
Prokaryotes do not undergo meiosis because they lack a nucleus and reproduce by cell division such as binary fission.
Fungi undergo meiosis during sexual reproduction.
The active site is the region of an enzyme where binding and catalysis occur, not the molecule acted upon.
A co-enzyme assists an enzyme but is not the molecule it acts on.
The molecule on which an enzyme acts is called its substrate.
A product is formed by the enzyme's reaction rather than acted upon.
Karl Lohmann discovered ATP in 1929.
Fritz Lipmann later helped establish ATP's role in energy transfer, but did not discover it.
Melvin Calvin is known for work on photosynthetic carbon fixation.
Hans Krebs is known for describing the citric acid cycle.
The textbook value is about 90%, not 95%.
About 90% of the water absorbed by plants is lost through transpiration.
The accepted approximate amount is not 85%.
The accepted approximate amount is not 80%.
Scientific names are not usually printed in English.
Scientific names are not usually printed in Greek.
Italics are a printing style, not a language.
Scientific names are Latin or latinized.
Deductions are conclusions drawn from evidence rather than the source of measured data.
A hypothesis is a proposed explanation to be tested.
Reporting communicates findings but does not generate the measurements.
Experiments are used to gather quantitative data.
Amoeba is a unicellular organism that lives independently, not in a colony.
Paramecium is a unicellular organism that lives independently, not in a colony.
Volvox is a colonial organism made up of many cooperating cells.
Euglena is generally a unicellular organism, not a colony.
Ribosomes synthesize proteins rather than digest food and waste.
Lysosomes contain enzymes that break down food particles and cellular waste.
Chromosomes carry genetic information rather than digesting materials.
Centrioles help organize microtubules during cell division.
Wilhelm Kühne first used the term enzyme.
Emil Fischer is known for the lock-and-key model of enzyme action.
Daniel Koshland proposed the induced-fit model of enzyme action.
Golgi is associated with the discovery of the Golgi apparatus, not the term enzyme.
In prophase I, chromosomes condense and the spindle begins to form.
In metaphase I, homologous chromosome pairs align at the cell equator.
During anaphase I, spindle fibres shorten to pull homologous chromosomes toward opposite poles.
In telophase I, chromosomes have reached the poles and the cell begins to divide.
